The big story, TS Champi. Champi continues to slowly strengthen east
of Guam as it moves west. The latest forecast track brings Champi
over northern Guam Sunday morning, with tropical storm force winds
arriving before midnight Saturday. Therefore, a Typhoon Warning was 
issued for Guam and Rota, with a Tropical Storm Warning issued for 
Tinian and Saipan, with a Typhoon Watch continuing in case Champi 
makes a turn to the north. The forecast for tonight and Saturday 
maintains the current drier pattern. However, that will change 
drastically as Champi approaches. Tropical storm force winds, 
increasing heavy showers and thunderstorms will move into the region 
Saturday evening. By Sunday morning, we can expect at least category 
2 typhoon force winds at Guam, category 1 at Rota and strong tropical
storm winds at Tinian and Saipan. Winds and convection will continue
over the islands through Sunday night, with tropical storm 
conditions possibly ending Sunday night, after midnight. After Champi
exits the region, a dry pattern looks to move into the region around
Monday and continuing through the end of the week. Residents of the 
Marianas should make sure that they are prepared for typhoon force
sustained winds of up to 105 mph. Stay safe and follow our forecasts
for any updates as they occur.

Marine...
Marine and surf conditions will deteriorate rapidly, beginning
Saturday evening as TS Champi approaches. A Typhoon Warning is in
effect for Guam and Rota waters, with a Tropical Storm Warning now 
in effect and Typhoon Watch remaining in effect for Tinian and 
Saipan. Combined seas will remain at or below 7 feet through 
Saturday morning, then begin to build as a large east swell from 
Champi enters the waters. As Champi moves through the waters, seas 
could reach as high as 35 feet near the center of Champi, depending 
on how much Champi strengthens. Seas will be lowest for Tinian and 
Saipan waters, but still reach around 19 feet as Champi moves 
through. The large seas produced by Champi are expected to produce 
dangerous/deadly surf and rip currents, as well as coastal flooding, 
with inundation of 5 feet or more near the eye of Champi, and as 
high as 1 to 3 feet at Tinian and Saipan. Surf could reach as high 
as 26 feet at Guam and 19 feet at Tinian and Saipan. Rota can expect 
around 20 feet. Seas could remain hazardous through Monday, after
Champi departs the region.

Tropical Systems...
As of 700 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Champi (29W) was
located near 12N152E, which is about 510 miles east-southeast of
Guam. It was moving west at 13 mph, with maximum sustained winds
having increased to 60 mph near the center. Champi is expected to 
make a slight turn toward the west-northwest with a slight increase 
in forward speed through Saturday. This general forecast track will 
take Champi close to, or over, Guam Sunday morning. Champi is 
expected to go through a period of rapid intensification over the 
next 24 hours, becoming a typhoon by Saturday and strengthening 
further thereafter. Winds and rain will come in rapidly, with winds 
becoming dangerous and life threatening very soon after onset. Do not
let a false sense of normalcy now dictate your actions tomorrow; 
prepare NOW! 

For more information, please refer to the bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, and by 
the National Weather Service in Tiyan, Guam under WMO header WTPQ32 
PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Tropical Storm Champi continues to move away from the region, which 
will allow showers to become isolated at Pohnpei Saturday night. 
Kosrae will mainly see isolated showers as well through the weekend, 
before increasing next week. However, at Majuro, the monsoon trough 
is lingering just to the north, with a another tropical circulation 
east of the Date Line poised to move into the region early next week.
This will keep scattered showers going through the forecast period 
there.

As Champi moves away, winds and seas will slowly decrease. Seas will
return to the 4 to 6 foot range at Pohnpei and Kosrae, remaining at 
these values for Majuro.

Western Micronesia...
The main forecast challenges were maximum wind gusts at Chuuk, and 
swell direction and height for Yap and Palau as current TS Champi 
passes north of there. For now, kept wind gusts to 30 knots at Chuuk 
but mentioned a few higher gusts could occur, but with some 
uncertainty as to when during the next 24 hours Champi begins its RI 
(Rapid Intensification) cycle. Therefore a special weather statement 
remains in place along with a Small Craft Advisory for hazardous 
seas. will be elevated Then at Yap, focus was placed on trying to 
refine swell heights and directions, while introducing them at Palau 
Tuesday. 

Otherwise, look for isolated shower coverage at Palau and Yap to
